verses.text: After Jesus finished teaching, he left Galilee and went to the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.
Large crowds followed him there, and he healed them.
Some Pharisees came to test him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?” they asked.
He answered, “Haven’t you read that the Creator made them male and female from the beginning?
He also said, ‘That’s why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.’
So they are no longer two but one. What God has joined together, no person should separate.”
They asked him, “Then why did Moses command a man to give his wife a divorce certificate and send her away?”
He told them, “Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts were hard. But that wasn’t how it was from the beginning.
I tell you, whoever divorces his wife, except because of sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery. Whoever marries a divorced woman also commits adultery.”
His disciples said to him, “If that’s how it is between a husband and wife, maybe it’s better not to marry.”
He answered, “Not everyone can accept this teaching—only those to whom it has been given.

Some are eunuchs because they were born that way. Some were made eunuchs by others. And some have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven. Whoever can accept this should accept it.”
Then people brought little children to Jesus so he could place his hands on them and pray. The disciples scolded them.
But Jesus said, “Let the children come to me. Don’t stop them, because the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to people like them.”
He placed his hands on them and then left there.
A man came to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why are you calling me good? No one is good except one—that is, God. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
“Which ones?” the man asked. Jesus said, “‘Don’t murder. Don’t commit adultery. Don’t steal. Don’t give false testimony.
Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
The young man said, “I’ve kept all these since I was young. What am I still missing?”
Jesus told him, “If you want to be perfect, go sell what you own and give the money to the poor. Then you’ll have treasure in heaven. After that, come follow me.”
When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he owned a lot.
Jesus told his disciples, “I’m telling you the truth: it’s hard for a rich person to enter the Kingdom of Heaven.
I’ll say it again: it’s easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter God’s Kingdom.”
When the disciples heard this, they were completely amazed. “Then who can be saved?” they asked.
Jesus looked at them and said, “People can’t do this, but with God all things are possible.”
Then Peter said, “Look, we left everything and followed you. What will we receive?”

Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: when everything is made new and the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, you who followed me will also sit on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
Everyone who has left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or land for my name will receive a hundred times as much and inherit eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first.”
